title: Web capability seam - stable tools over multiple providers
summary: Web access is one capability: a web service owns provider registration and selection, providers register search or fetch backends, and one tool package owns the model-facing web_search and web_fetch schemas. Providers never register tools.
firstReason: This is the capability-seam pattern applied to web access; it keeps the model contract stable while search vendors with very different response shapes come and go.

title: Offer web_search and web_fetch only while the selected provider is ready
summary: The web search and web fetch tools are offered to the model at each step only if the selected provider has a credential for the current model route. The check reads configuration only and makes no network call.
firstReason: Otherwise a session is offered a tool whose every call fails with a credential error. A per-step readiness check on the provider interface is cheap and language-neutral.

title: Plugin CLIs by absolute path in runtime context
summary: A plugin that installs a vendor command-line tool outside PATH registers its absolute path, and the harness tells the model in required runtime context to run it by that path. The harness does not change the environment that commands run in.
firstReason: The model must run the plugin's own copy, and altering PATH for every shell would change how all commands behave. Telling the model is the least invasive mechanism and is language-neutral.

title: Runtime download of upstream skills
summary: Vendor-published skill guides are not copied into the repository. A plugin pins them by repository, commit, size and digest; the host downloads the archive when the plugin loads, verifies it and caches it under the harness home.
firstReason: It avoids redistributing another company's content and keeps large vendored files out of the source tree; that reason holds for a Go binary. A failed download must not block account sign-in, and the download host is configurable for offline installs.

title: Web provider selection - independent menus over registered providers
summary: Users choose the search provider and the fetch provider independently, from the lists of providers registered in the host. By default search follows the conversation's model route and fetch uses local HTTP.
firstReason: One combined control tied fetch billing and access policy to the search choice, and could not show providers added by other plugins. An observable provider registry with two independent selections ports directly.

title: MCP connector accounts in the connector account registry
summary: An adapter service (`ctx.mcpAccounts`) registers each OAuth MCP server as a connector account under the key `mcp:<server>`, reads its status from the MCP manager and maps the manager's states to the shared connect, sign-out and retry operations.
firstReason: One adapter in place of per-connector account code removes the 23 strings and the state handling that every connector repeated. The adapter is plain host logic over two services.

title: Malformed charset recovery prefers UTF-8
summary: When a response declares an unusable charset such as `utf-8,gbk`, the fetch provider looks for a UTF-8 label inside the declaration and, if one is present, decodes strictly as UTF-8; otherwise it fails before reading the body. Invalid UTF-8 is rejected, not guessed.
firstReason: Real servers send malformed charset headers, and a strict decoder would reject readable pages. The rule is a small explicit heuristic that a Go decoder can apply the same way.

title: Settings-driven MCP server manager
summary: A manager service owns the live-updatable list of MCP servers and reconciles a fleet of ordinary MCP client instances, so servers can be added, tested, enabled and removed from Settings at runtime. Plugins register servers as effects that end with the plugin, and the client owns connection supervision, status and startup budgets.
firstReason: Runtime management of MCP servers with per-server status is a product requirement. MCP is also the protocol for tool-only plugins in DH-ADR-4, so this manager becomes more central in the Go design.

title: On-demand MCP tool loading
summary: An MCP server marked `toolLoading: on-demand` keeps its tools out of the registry. The model sees one loader tool per server and a catalog of tool names with the first line of each description in the system prompt, and loaded tools register in a scope owned by that agent.
firstReason: One hosted server can cost over 200,000 characters of tool definitions on every request; loading on demand removes that cost without a new event type. Agent-scoped registration released on disposal is the cordis model.

title: Direct DeepSeek Search and Fetch APIs
summary: DeepSeek's dedicated Search and Fetch APIs are implemented as providers behind the existing `web_search` and `web_fetch` tools, registered as `deepseek-search-api` and `deepseek-fetch-api` and selected independently. Retrieval no longer needs an auxiliary model request per query.
firstReason: It removes a wasted generation per search and fits the web capability seam, in which providers are swappable behind fixed tool schemas.
